questions_and_answers.question: What tense is primarily used for narrating consecutive events in German?
Which forms can past participles serve as, aside from being part of verb phrases?
What suffix is used to form adjectives from nouns in German, similar to -ish in English?
Which suffix added to numbers forms time expressions like 'once' or 'twice' in German?
In what type of clause is the past tense frequently used instead of the perfect phrase?

answers.answer: Subordinate clauses introduced by als, da, or weil

questions_and_answers.question: Give an example of a participle used as an adjective in German.
Which German word for 'French' is derived from a noun via -isch?
What English suffix corresponds to German -lich when forming adjectives?
Which suffix forms time expressions ending in -s, such as 'abends'?
Which German sentence means 'Because the car only cost ... DM we bought it on the spot'?

answers.answer: Weil das Auto nur 2000 DM kostete, haben wir es auf der Stelle gekauft.

articles.text:
D. DERIVATIVE ADJECTIVES AND ADVERBS.
In Unit 11 we called attention to a number of DERIVATIVE NOUNS, that is, nouns formed from verbs, adjectives and other nouns.
The use of the past participle as an adjective or adverb discussed above represents the simplest type of DERIVATIVE ADJECTIVE formation.
There is no change in form from PARTICIPLE to ADJECTIVE or ADVERB. This is similar to the use of the infinitive as a noun noted in Unit 11.
Most derivative adjectives and adverbs however are formed by the addition of a suffix to other parts of speech.
1. A few German adjectives and adverbs are formed from nouns by the addition of the suffix -isch, sometimes with umlaut.
Compare the English suffixes -ish and -ic: girl-ish, diplomat-ic.
The adjectives and adverbs following have both occurred in the basic sentences to date:
der Franzose -> französisch (Frenchman -> French)
das Telephon -> telephonisch (telephone -> by or on the telephone)
Following this pattern form adjectives or adverbs from these nouns: der Diplomat, das Kind, die Stadt.
2. Many German adjectives and adverbs are formed from nouns by the addition of the suffix -lich, sometimes with umlaut of the stem vowel.
Compare the English suffix -ly: man-ly, hour-ly. The following adjectives and adverbs have occurred in the basic sentences to date:
das Gemüt -> gemütlich (feelings -> cozy)
die Natur -> natürlich (nature -> naturally, of course)
der Tag -> täglich (day -> daily, every day)
der Umstand -> umständlich (circumstance -> involved, complicated)
Notice that the derived forms do not always resemble the original noun closely in meaning.
Following the pattern established above form adjectives or adverbs from the following nouns which have occurred in your basic sentences:
der Beruf, der Monat, der Zahnarzt, der Bruder, der Sommer, der Freund, der Staat, das Bild, das Haus, das Geschäft, das Jahr, die Hand, die Heimat, die Wirtschaft, die Person.
The following derivatives are slightly irregular: das Ende -> endlich (end -> finally); der Name -> nämlich (name -> namely); die Stunde -> stündlich (hour -> hourly); die Woche -> wöchentlich (week -> weekly).
3. A few German adjectives and adverbs are formed from other adjectives in the same way.
Compare the English suffix -ly in formations such as briefly, recently:
blau -> bläulich (blue -> bluish)
froh -> fröhlich (glad, happy -> merry, merrily)
kurz -> kürzlich (short, brief -> recently)
neu -> neulich (new -> recently)
According to this pattern form adjectives or adverbs from the following adjectives: bekannt, ganz, grün, schwer.
4. A number of German adjectives and adverbs are formed from nouns by the addition of the suffix -ig, sometimes with umlaut of the stem vowel and elision of a final unstressed syllable.
Compare the English suffix -y in words such as rain-y, wind-y.
Examples: der Durst -> durstig (thirst -> thirsty); die Farbe -> farbig (color -> colored, colorful); das Wasser -> wässerig (water -> watery); die Zeit -> zeitig (time -> timely, on time).
According to this pattern form adjectives or adverbs from the following nouns which have occurred in your basic sentences: der Hunger, der Käse, das Gespräch, das Gebirge, die Milch, die Wolke.
